questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of a sound wave?
choices: It travels in a straight line
It can travel through a vacuum
It is a transverse wave
It needs a medium to travel
questions.solution: Sound waves are mechanical waves that require a medium to propagate, which makes 'It needs a medium to travel' the correct answer. Sound does not travel in a straight line because it can diffract around objects. It cannot travel through a vacuum since there is no medium to carry the vibrations. Additionally, sound is a longitudinal wave, not a transverse one.

questions.stem: Why do we perceive some sounds as high-pitched and others as low-pitched?
choices: Because of the speed of sound in the medium
Because of the frequency of the sound waves
Because of the amplitude of the sound waves
Because of the loudness of the sound waves
questions.solution: We perceive some sounds as high-pitched and others as low-pitched because of the frequency of the sound waves. High-pitched sounds have higher frequency, while low-pitched sounds have lower frequency. The option 'Because of the speed of sound in the medium' is incorrect because speed does not directly affect pitch. The option 'Because of the amplitude of the sound waves' is incorrect because amplitude affects loudness, not pitch. The option 'Because of the loudness of the sound waves' is incorrect because loudness is related to amplitude, not pitch.

questions.stem: In a room, the reflected sound reaches the ear 0.05 seconds after its production. What type of sound effect is this?
choices: Echo
Reverberation
Reflection
Diffraction
questions.solution: Reverberation occurs when sound reflects off surfaces and reaches the ear within a short time, typically less than 0.1 seconds. Since the delay here is 0.05 seconds, it is classified as reverberation. An echo requires a longer delay, and reflection and diffraction are not specific sound effects in this context.

questions.stem: Why does a sound wave with a larger amplitude travel a larger distance before its intensity reduces to zero?
choices: Because it carries more energy
Because it has a higher frequency
Because it travels faster
Because it has a shorter wavelength
questions.solution: A sound wave with a larger amplitude carries more energy, which allows it to travel a larger distance before its intensity reduces to zero. Higher frequency and shorter wavelength relate to the wave's characteristics but not the distance it can travel. Faster speed would not necessarily mean the wave lasts longer, as intensity depends on energy dissipation over distance.

questions.stem: In the vacuum bell jar experiment, the electric bell is observed to ring even when no sound is heard. What does this indicate about the nature of sound?
choices: Sound can travel without a medium
Sound is a form of energy that can exist independently
Sound requires a medium to propagate
Sound is produced only when there is air
questions.solution: The observation that the electric bell rings but produces no sound in a vacuum indicates that sound requires a medium to propagate. Without air, vibrations cannot travel, so no sound is heard. The other options are incorrect because sound cannot travel through a vacuum, and it is not independent of a medium or limited to air.
